patients.label: 49-year-old man with atopic dermatitis and refractory chronic external otitis (external ear eczema)

identity_evidence.quote: This case report describes a 49-year-old male patient

attribution_limitations: The article names the diagnosis both as chronic external otitis (abstract) and as external ear eczema (introduction and discussion) and never states that they are the same entity.
The source does not say whether betamethasone valerate and gentamicin sulfate are one combined ointment or two separate ointments.
The text says allergy testing showed high sensitization to environmental and food antigens, but Table 2 lists only environmental allergens (mites, dust, pollens, molds, animal epithelium).

Table 1 and Table 2 give no dates; only the text says the IgE and TARC values were measured following dupilumab therapy. TARC is printed in pg/dL and IgE as IU/mL in Table 1 but allergen IgE as Ua/mL in Table 2.

The authors attribute persistent refractoriness likely to habitual ear cleaning and credit delgocitinib with suppressing IL-31 and ending habitual ear manipulation; no IL-31 level or change in ear-cleaning behavior is measured in the case.
Figure captions give right and left laterality for the otoscopic findings, whereas the narrative text states the external auditory canal findings without laterality.

evidence.quote: Findings of the right external auditory canal at the initial visit. A significant amount of scales is adherent to the external auditory canal (red arrowheads), which appears erythematous. Erythema and scales are also observed on the tympanic membrane (yellow arrowhead).

Findings of the left external auditory canal at the initial visit. A significant amount of scales is adherent to the external auditory canal (red arrowheads), which appears erythematous. Scales are also observed on the tympanic membrane (yellow arrowhead).

Findings of the right external auditory canal after one month of treatment. Erythema of the external auditory canal has improved, and the scaling has subsided (red arrowheads). However, the tympanic membrane remains erythematous (yellow arrowhead).

Findings of the left external auditory canal after one month of treatment. Both erythema and scaling of the external auditory canal have subsided (red arrowheads). The tympanic membrane still shows slight erythema (yellow arrowhead).
Findings of the right external auditory canal after one year. Findings are normal in both the external auditory canal (red arrowheads) and the tympanic membrane (yellow arrowhead).
Findings of the left external auditory canal after one year. Findings are normal in both the external auditory canal (red arrowheads) and the tympanic membrane (yellow arrowhead).

limitations: Tables 1 to 3 carry no collection dates; only the narrative ties the IgE and TARC values to the period following dupilumab therapy.
Discussion statements about IL-31 suppression, the likely role of habitual ear cleaning and the mechanism of delgocitinib are author interpretation and are not recorded as patient facts.
Figure pixels are reviewed in the separate visual target.

claims.text: A 49-year-old man with atopic dermatitis, bronchial asthma, hypertension, cataracts and glaucoma, with multiple drug and food allergies, presented with persistent ear pruritus. Atopic dermatitis had been managed since childhood, and dupilumab fourteen months earlier markedly improved the trunk lesions, but severe ear pruritus persisted despite topical steroid ear drops and steroid ointments, prompting referral.
